archetypes.name: Mid-Market Fashion D2C + Omnichannel
archetypes.brandClass: Indigo Road / Marine Layer / Outdoor Voices / Reformation / Buck Mason / Allbirds-class — DTC-native fashion brand that opened physical stores.

archetypes.name: SMB Full-Service Restaurant
archetypes.brainPosture: do-it-for-me by default, escalate on ambiguity
archetypes.brandClass: Neighborhood independent or small-chain restaurant — Italian / steakhouse / casual American / gastropub / craft-beer-bar class. 1–3 locations, $2–8M annual GPV typical. Owner-operator-led; the owner is also the GM at the flagship location.

archetypes.name: Mid-Market Subscription SaaS (direct billing)
archetypes.brandClass: Notion / Linear / ClickUp / Airtable / Calendly / Loom / Webflow class — productivity SaaS sold to teams + individuals; OR Substack / Patreon / OnlyFans-class creator-subscription; OR Calm / Headspace / NYT-Cooking-class consumer-subscription apps. Mid-market SaaS at $10M–$300M ARR/GPV; not yet enterprise-led but no longer founder-mode.

archetypes.name: Mid-Market B2B Distributor (NET terms, L2/L3 data)
archetypes.brandClass: Industrial supplier (Grainger-class small / mid-tier), restaurant supply (US Foods sub-distributor class), auto-parts wholesaler, medical-supply distributor, educational-textbook distributor, MRO supplier — B2B with NET-30/NET-60 invoicing, large-ticket transactions ($500-$50,000+ per invoice typical), purchasing-card acceptance, ACH for large invoices.

archetypes.name: SMB Quick-Service Restaurant
archetypes.brainPosture: do-it-for-me by default, escalate on ambiguity
archetypes.brandClass: Independent fast-casual (taqueria, sandwich shop, pizza shop, juice bar, salad bowl class), franchisee operating 1-3 locations of a national QSR brand, or small local chain (4-8 locations). 1-3 locations typical at this tier; $1.5-7M per location annual GPV.

archetypes.name: SMB Coffee/Café
archetypes.brandClass: Independent coffee shop, regional small-chain (3-8 locations) like Blue Bottle-class at the SMB tier, neighborhood roastery, espresso-bar-with-merchandise. Very high transaction count, very small average ticket ($5-$25). Loyalty is the unit-economics lever; loyalty-app spend captures meaningful share of total volume.

archetypes.name: Micro-SMB Personal Services (salon/spa)
archetypes.brandClass: Independent hair salon (1-3 stylist chairs), nail salon, day-spa, massage therapy practice, esthetician studio, fitness studio (yoga/pilates/barre at small scale). Owner-operator-led; often the owner is also a practicing stylist/therapist. <$1M annual GPV.

archetypes.name: PayFac-served Vertical-SaaS Sub-merchant
archetypes.brandClass: A merchant who takes payments embedded in a vertical-SaaS platform — gym using Mindbody class platform, salon using Vagaro class, healthcare clinic using Athenahealth class, tutoring service using ClassDojo Pay class, fitness studio using ClassPass-style class, dentist using OpenDental Pay class, real-estate brokerage using Avail-class. The vertical-SaaS platform acts as the PayFac (Stripe Connect / Adyen MarketPay / Worldpay PayFac-as-a-service class) and the merchant is a "sub-merchant" within the platform's master account.

archetypes.name: Marketplace Sub-merchant (rideshare/delivery/services-marketplace seller-of-record)
archetypes.brainPosture: co-pilot-with-agency (sub-seller has very limited control; marketplace is canonical authority)
archetypes.gpvBand: $100k-$10M (varies; aggregated marketplace volume can be 10x sub-merchant individual)
archetypes.brandClass: Drivers/sellers/service-providers earning income through a marketplace — Uber/Lyft drivers earning fares, DoorDash dashers, Etsy sellers, Airbnb hosts (not the marketplace itself, but a seller within it), TaskRabbit taskers, Fiverr freelancers, Postmates couriers, Wag dogwalkers. The marketplace operates as the seller-of-record (or facilitates per state marketplace-facilitator law) and the seller is the sub-merchant in the marketplace's master-merchant account.

archetypes.name: Enterprise Hospitality Omnichannel
archetypes.brandClass: "Marriott-class regional flag with 38 hotels + 12 standalone restaurants + 8 spas", "Hyatt-class luxury portfolio with 22 properties × 4 brands across 8 countries".

archetypes.name: Enterprise Retail Multi-Location
archetypes.brandClass: "regional department store with 95 stores + e-com + outlet-marketplace + endless-aisle", "specialty-retail chain with 200 stores + e-com + Faire-class B2B-marketplace + 3PL fulfillment".

archetypes.name: Enterprise Healthcare System
archetypes.brandClass: "regional health-system with 6 hospitals + 22 clinics + 4 pharmacies + research + lab + telehealth across 3 states" or "academic-medical-center-class with hospital + research + faculty-practice-plan + 340B drug program".

archetypes.name: ISO-channel SMB Mixed Retail
archetypes.brandClass: "Powell's Books-class neighborhood bookstore", "Acme Hardware-class corner hardware store", or "Stinker's Outdoor-class single-location outdoor outfitter" — independent brick-and-mortar with one or two locations, who also runs a basic e-com store (Shopify / WooCommerce / BigCommerce-class on hosted-checkout or plugin).

archetypes.name: ISO-channel SMB Personal Services
archetypes.brandClass: "neighborhood salon-class" or "single-suite massage-therapy-class" or "single-location dance-studio-class" — owner-operator with 2–8 service providers, mostly returning local customers, mix of walk-in and booked appointments. Often includes recurring members or package-buyers.

archetypes.name: Mid-Market Healthcare Provider
archetypes.brandClass: "Direct Primary Care medical group with 12 locations + telehealth", "DSO-class dental support organization with 18 practices", "regional behavioral-health platform with subscription-membership + per-visit billing".

archetypes.name: Mid-Market Marketplace-Enabled Brand
archetypes.brandClass: "Reverb-class musical-instrument marketplace operating direct + 800 third-party sellers", "regional B2B wholesale marketplace with 1,200 brand-side sellers + 5,000 buyer-side accounts".

archetypes.name: PayFac Marketplace Seller
archetypes.brandClass: "Etsy-class indie jewelry seller", "Faire-class B2B wholesale crafts seller", "Gumroad-class digital-product creator" — solo-to-5-person operation, sells primarily through one or more marketplace platforms (sometimes with a side own-site), funds flow through PayFac aggregator with marketplace fee + PayFac fee deducted.

archetypes.name: Marquee Strategic-QSR
archetypes.gpvBand: $1B+ GPV (multi-brand QSR holding company; 5,000-50,000 units global)

archetypes.name: Marquee Marketplace
archetypes.gpvBand: $1B+ GPV (multi-category marketplace; 1M-10M+ active sellers; 100M+ active buyers)

archetypes.name: Marquee Healthcare System
archetypes.gpvBand: $1B+ GPV (integrated delivery network; 50+ hospitals + 1,000+ ambulatory + research + payer-side; $20B-$100B+ revenue)

archetypes.name: Cannabis Dispensary (state-licensed)
archetypes.gpvBand: $1M-$10M GPV (single-state or limited-multi-state operator; 1-15 retail locations)

archetypes.name: Firearms Dealer (FFL-licensed)
archetypes.gpvBand: $1M-$50M GPV (single-store FFL or small chain; 1-25 retail locations)

archetypes.name: Buying-Group / Purchasing Co-op
archetypes.gpvBand: $100M-$5B aggregate co-op GPV (200-5,000 member stores; individual member $1M-$30M)

jtbds.title: Migrate live e-com checkout from incumbent processor to new processor without conversion regression
jtbds.when: finance has signed the deal to switch processors and engineering has stood up sandbox parity,
jtbds.iWantTo: cut over the live e-com drop-in checkout in a controlled rollout with measurable approval-rate parity (or lift) versus the prior 30-day baseline,
jtbds.soICan: capture the cost-of-acceptance savings without taking a one-time conversion hit that wipes out the negotiated savings

metadata.trigger: Sandbox certification complete + pre-cutover checklist 95% green + cutover window scheduled (state transition: `merchant.cutover_status = 'ready'`)
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Backend dev lead
metadata.workaround: Manually compare daily approval-rate dashboards from the old processor vs new for 14 days post-cutover; rollback if drop > 1.5pp
metadata.successMetric: Approval rate within ±0.5pp of prior 30-day baseline at end of week 1; cumulative basket-value variance ≤ 0.3% over 14 days
metadata.failureMode: Silent approval-rate drop on a specific BIN range or APM → revenue loss = (delta-pp × monthly volume × AOV) for the duration before detection (typical: $30k–$200k for a fashion D2C in the $50M GPV band before a 7-day-late detection)
metadata.failureFrequency: ~30% of mid-market migrations show >1pp regression in week 1 that goes undiagnosed for 5–10 days
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (industry data: McKinsey 2024 cost-of-acceptance survey + Buck Mason cutover post-mortem referenced in `06-research/competitors.md`)

jtbds.title: Provision POS at a new physical store on day 0 without weekend-launch downtime
jtbds.when: a new retail store has a confirmed grand-opening date,
jtbds.iWantTo: provision POS terminals, configure tip/tender/refund permissions, integrate with the OMS for inventory + omnichannel returns, and certify card-present + tap + wallet within one calendar week,
jtbds.soICan: open on schedule without manual workarounds (e.g., paper sales-then-batch-entry) that produce reconciliation chaos for weeks

metadata.trigger: Calendar event: `store.opening_date - 14 days` (scheduled tick, phase boundary)
metadata.frequency: 2–6× per year for an actively-expanding mid-market brand
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Store Operations Manager
metadata.workaround: Director of Payments personally babysits the integration via Slack with the POS vendor's CSM; one or two stores per year still launch with at least one terminal "configured wrong" (wrong MCC mapping, wrong tip preset)
metadata.successMetric: All store terminals certified for card-present, tap, and wallet 48h before opening; first-day transaction success rate ≥ 99.0%
metadata.failureMode: Tap or wallet not enabled on day 1 → 8–15% of would-be transactions fall back to card-swipe + signature + slower line; customer satisfaction drops on opening weekend; ratio impact via NPS hit + small but real revenue loss
metadata.failureFrequency: ~15% of new-store openings have at least one terminal misconfigured at go-live
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (industry pattern across ICR / Forrester store-rollout studies)

jtbds.title: Configure cross-channel tokenization so the same customer's card works in-store, online, and on the mobile app
jtbds.when: the brand wants to enable seamless omnichannel (BOPIS, ship-from-store, return-to-store, mobile-checkout-pickup-in-store),
jtbds.iWantTo: ensure a single network-token (or processor-token) is propagated across POS + e-com + mobile so the customer's stored card is recognized everywhere,
jtbds.soICan: deliver true single-identity payments without forcing customers to re-enter cards at each surface, and so refunds-to-original-card work across channels

metadata.trigger: Brand kicks off omnichannel program (state transition: `merchant.omnichannel_status = 'enabled'`); or new mobile app launch (phase boundary)
metadata.frequency: 1× per major omnichannel rollout; periodic re-validation when card-network token spec changes (~annually)
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Mobile dev lead
metadata.workaround: Customers re-enter cards on each channel; manual exception flow when a customer wants to refund-to-original-card across channels (often handled as gift-card or store-credit instead)
metadata.successMetric: ≥ 70% of returning multi-channel customers have an active network token on file across ≥ 2 channels within 90 days; refund-to-original-card succeeds across channels in ≥ 95% of attempts
metadata.failureMode: Customer presents stored card in-store that the POS doesn't recognize (despite e-com having it tokenized) → decline or fallback to card-swipe; customer trust loss + checkout-line delay; cross-channel refund forced to gift-card → CFPB complaint risk if customer didn't agree
metadata.failureFrequency: ~40% of omnichannel mid-market brands have token-propagation gaps that surface at refund time
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (Visa Token Service whitepaper + EMVCo Tokenization Specification public doc)

jtbds.title: Integrate fraud-tooling vendor without false-positive spike during onboarding window
jtbds.when: swapping or first-installing a third-party fraud screening vendor,
jtbds.iWantTo: tune rules to merchant-specific patterns (returning-customer LTV, AOV bands, geo-mix, fashion-specific signals like cart-velocity for limited drops) before the vendor's default model fires on legitimate customers,
jtbds.soICan: avoid an onboarding-week false-positive spike that costs real revenue and trains customers to think "this brand doesn't work."

metadata.frequency: 1× per fraud vendor switch (typical: every 2–4 years); periodic re-tuning quarterly
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Fraud Vendor CSM
metadata.workaround: Run vendor in shadow mode (no enforcement) for 2 weeks; manually review false-positive reports; adjust 5–10 rules by hand
metadata.successMetric: First-week post-cutover false-positive rate ≤ 1.5× shadow-mode baseline; legitimate-customer decline-rate increase ≤ 0.3pp
metadata.failureMode: Vendor's default model declines a recurring high-LTV cohort (e.g., gift-givers buying limited drops with new BIN) → CS ticket spike + social-media complaints + revenue loss = (declined-volume × AOV × 30–50% non-retry rate)
metadata.failureFrequency: ~50% of fraud-vendor cutovers produce a measurable false-positive spike in week 1
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (Riskified / Signifyd / Forter merchant onboarding playbooks; public BFCM 2023 Adyen Fraud Trends report)

jtbds.title: Wire payment-data feed to ERP for finance-team reconciliation without breaking the chart of accounts
jtbds.when: finance demands a daily summary that ties to the GL by deposit, by store, by channel, by APM,
jtbds.iWantTo: map the processor's settlement file format and webhook events to the merchant's specific chart of accounts (with their custom dimensions: store-id, channel, APM, marketplace),
jtbds.soICan: stop the weekly back-and-forth between payments and finance over "where did this $X go" and have finance close books on time

metadata.trigger: User-initiated: finance team requests a new GL-feed (typically at fiscal-year start or after an ERP re-implementation)
metadata.frequency: 1–2× per year (at year-start, after ERP changes, or when finance re-orgs)
metadata.actor: Finance Controller + Director of Payments + Backend dev
metadata.workaround: Daily CSV export from processor portal → manual transformation in Excel → manual upload to ERP; 1–2 hours per finance person per day
metadata.successMetric: Daily GL feed reconciles to processor settlement file within 0.05% variance; finance close happens within 5 business days after month-end (was 8–10 days before)
metadata.failureMode: Mapping drift (e.g., a new APM added without a GL line) → unposted entries → SOX audit trail issue + finance manual rework + close delayed = ~20–40 hours of finance time per occurrence + audit notes
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per quarter mapping drift goes undetected for 1+ months
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (NetSuite SuiteBilling integration patterns; SOX 404 internal-controls public-company filings)

jtbds.title: BFCM peak window — pre-warmed launch brain
jtbds.when: Black Friday + Cyber Monday window opens (Nov 1 → Dec 5 typical scope),
jtbds.iWantTo: pre-warm thresholds, monitor every 5 minutes, alert on any out-of-band metric (approval rate, fraud rate, latency, decline reason concentration), and offer immediate recommended responses (route-shift, fraud-rule-relax, capacity-add),
jtbds.soICan: survive the highest-stakes 5 weeks of the year without revenue regressions

metadata.actor: Director of Payments + entire ops team (24/7 during peak hours)
metadata.successMetric: Zero major regressions go undetected > 5 minutes; no manual war-room work past 1am; revenue lift vs baseline-day pattern ≥ projected
metadata.failureMode: Missed BFCM regression → large revenue loss = (delta-pp × peak-hourly-volume × duration); examples: silent EU-card decline cliff after token-vendor change, mobile app crash on iOS X.Y, fraud-vendor over-aggressive on returning-customer cohort
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per year a mid-market brand has a peak-window regression that's caught hours late
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (mvp-scope.md Slice A killer demo: BFCM launch brain)

jtbds.title: Processor outage — detect, notify, route to backup APM
jtbds.when: the primary processor's auth success rate drops below 50% across the merchant's MIDs (or the network publishes an incident),
jtbds.iWantTo: detect within 5 minutes, alert ops, recommend fallback (alternate APM, alternate route, customer-facing message),
jtbds.soICan: minimize revenue loss during outage rather than discovering it via customer complaints

metadata.trigger: Threshold crossing: auth success rate < 50% over 5-min window across all MIDs OR webhook event: `processor.incident`
metadata.frequency: 1–4× per year (typical: minor incidents) + 1× per ~3 years (major outage)
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Backend dev (24/7 on-call)
metadata.workaround: Hand-on-pulse monitoring + processor's ad-hoc Slack channel
metadata.successMetric: Detection time ≤ 5 min; fallback-route-active time ≤ 15 min if applicable; revenue saved during incident
metadata.failureMode: Outage detected late → revenue loss compounds; or misdiagnosed (assumed processor outage when it's a network issue) → wrong fallback
metadata.failureFrequency: 1–2 incidents per year per merchant get fingered late

jtbds.title: Fraud ring detected (cross-merchant pattern or single-merchant burst)
jtbds.when: the fraud-vendor (or internal AnomalyAgent) flags a suspected fraud ring (multiple cards from same device-cluster, geo-cluster, or referral-cluster all hitting in sequence),
jtbds.iWantTo: receive a single consolidated alert with the ring-shape (which dimensions cluster, who's affected), recommended action (rule-based block, manual review, escalate-to-network),
jtbds.soICan: stop the ring fast rather than declining cards one-at-a-time

metadata.trigger: Anomaly-detection signal from fraud-vendor or AnomalyAgent
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Fraud Vendor CSM + InvestigationAgent
metadata.workaround: Reactive; identified hours after the fact
metadata.successMetric: Ring-detection time ≤ 30 min from first-card; ring-shape correctness ≥ 80%; recommended-action match expert ≥ 75%
metadata.failureMode: Ring not detected → multi-card loss; or false-ring-flag → blocking a legitimate cohort
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per year a ring is detected hours late

jtbds.title: PCI-scope expansion event (new POS hardware reconnects scope)
jtbds.when: new POS hardware is provisioned that touches card-data-not-yet-in-scope,
jtbds.iWantTo: detect the scope-touch, draft an attestation update + remediation plan, and route to compliance team,
jtbds.soICan: prevent annual-attestation invalidation that's triggered by scope-creep

metadata.trigger: State transition: new POS-hardware-class added to merchant's stack
metadata.workaround: Annual attestation review catches it (months late)
metadata.successMetric: Scope-touch detected within 7 days; attestation update drafted within 30 days
metadata.failureMode: Scope-creep undetected → annual attestation invalidated → reassessment cost + program enrollment risk
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per 2 years a scope expansion is missed

jtbds.title: Data-breach detection + response (merchant-side or vendor-side)
jtbds.when: a data breach is detected (merchant's own systems, fraud-vendor's systems, processor's systems, or e-com-platform's systems) that potentially affects payment-card or PII data of the brand's customers,
jtbds.iWantTo: receive immediate cross-functional alert, draft customer-notification per state-residency rules (GDPR / CCPA / NY-SHIELD / Massachusetts / etc.), draft regulator-notification packages, and coordinate with security + legal + comms,
jtbds.soICan: meet 72h breach-notification windows under multiple regulatory regimes and preserve brand trust through transparent + compliant disclosure

metadata.trigger: Crisis event: breach indicator (security-substrate alert / vendor-disclosure / external researcher contact / press inquiry)
metadata.frequency: 0–1× per year (rare but consequential — Taleb black-swan)
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Compliance + Legal + Security + Comms (often CEO involvement)
metadata.workaround: Per-event scramble; many brands have a written incident-response plan but execution under pressure is uneven
metadata.successMetric: Customer-notification draft within 24h of confirmation; regulator-notification within 48h; full-disclosure within 72h per highest-applicable-regulation
metadata.failureMode: Missed regulatory deadline → fine ($100–$50,000 per affected customer under HIPAA-class; equivalent under GDPR / state laws) + brand damage that compounds for years; or premature disclosure of unconfirmed breach → customer panic + class-action invitation
metadata.failureFrequency: ~50% of merchants who experience a breach miss at least one state's deadline
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (Taleb-fragility black-swan pattern surfaced by debate-mode panel review; GDPR Article 33–34, CCPA breach-disclosure rules public)

jtbds.title: Annual processor contract review — cost-of-acceptance for renegotiation
jtbds.when: processor contract renewal is 90–180 days out,
jtbds.iWantTo: receive a comprehensive cost-of-acceptance analysis with year-over-year trends, peer-benchmark comparison (where available), and identification of negotiable cost levers (volume tiering, MID consolidation, fee waivers),
jtbds.soICan: enter renegotiation prepared rather than letting the processor lead

metadata.actor: Director of Payments + Finance Controller + (sometimes) Procurement
metadata.successMetric: Renegotiation outcome reflects analysis ≥ 70% of recommended levers; cost-savings achieved ≥ 5% of total cost-of-acceptance
metadata.failureMode: Misframed renegotiation → poor outcome → 2–3 years of suboptimal cost
metadata.failureFrequency: ~50% of mid-market contract renewals are sub-optimally negotiated

jtbds.title: Year-end 1099-K filings + sales-tax filings
jtbds.when: fiscal year-end approaches,
jtbds.iWantTo: prepare 1099-K filings for any marketplace-facilitator obligations + cross-state sales-tax filings + audit-package documentation,
jtbds.soICan: meet regulatory deadlines without a year-end fire drill

metadata.actor: Finance Controller + Tax CPA + Director of Payments
metadata.workaround: Manual; takes 2–4 weeks of finance-team time
metadata.successMetric: All filings completed by deadline; no penalty notices; audit-package complete
metadata.failureMode: Missed filing → state penalty + interest; incomplete audit-package → audit-cycle delays
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per 2 years a filing or audit-package issue

jtbds.title: Regulator inquiry response (CFPB / FTC / state AG / card-network)
jtbds.when: a regulator (CFPB / FTC / state AG / state DFI / card-network compliance) issues an inquiry, request-for-documentation, or a complaint forwarded from a customer,
jtbds.iWantTo: assemble the relevant transaction history, communications, policy documents, and prior-resolution evidence; draft a compliance-tone response within the regulator's deadline; and coordinate with Legal + Compliance,
jtbds.soICan: respond accurately and on-time without escalating an inquiry into an enforcement action

metadata.trigger: User-initiated: regulator inquiry received (mail / portal / email / phone-followed-up-in-writing)
metadata.frequency: 0–4× per year for a typical mid-market D2C
metadata.workaround: Manual scramble per inquiry; document-collection + drafting + legal-review takes 2–4 weeks
metadata.successMetric: Response submitted on time 100%; document completeness ≥ 95% per inquiry-type checklist; no follow-up "missing information" requests
metadata.failureMode: Late response or incomplete documentation → inquiry escalates to formal investigation → enforcement action + fine + multi-year monitoring; brand-reputation impact via public-disclosure obligations
metadata.failureFrequency: ~25% of mid-market regulator inquiries get late or incomplete responses
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (Taleb fragility + Porter competitive-positioning panel surfacing; CFPB / FTC public enforcement patterns)

jtbds.title: Watch first 72 hours after a major launch (new APM, new region, processor cutover, mobile-app launch)
jtbds.when: a launch window opens (cutover hour, APM enabled in production, mobile-app first-version live),
jtbds.iWantTo: monitor approval rate, decline reasons, dispute formation, ticket arrivals, and reconciliation variance every 15–60 minutes against pre-defined thresholds,
jtbds.soICan: catch a regression in hours, not days, and roll back before damage compounds

metadata.trigger: Phase boundary: `launch_window.opens` (e.g., new APM `production_active = true`, processor cutover hour, mobile app first-version released)
metadata.actor: Director of Payments + on-call dev (BFCM: full ops team)
metadata.workaround: Director of Payments personally watches a custom Looker dashboard + Slack-alerts manually configured; sleep is optional
metadata.successMetric: All material regressions detected within 60 minutes; rollback (or fix-forward) decision communicated within 90 minutes of first signal
metadata.failureMode: Regression detected at +24h instead of +1h → 23h of compound damage; revenue loss = (regression-rate × hourly-volume × 23h); examples include silent EU-card decline cliff after new APM enable, or mobile-app token-refresh bug
metadata.failureFrequency: ~25% of launches have a material issue the merchant only catches at +24h or later
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (mvp-scope.md Slice A killer demo: BFCM launch brain)

jtbds.title: Validate mobile-app payments SDK across iOS / Android / OS-versions on day-1 production
jtbds.when: the brand's mobile app v1.0 (or a major payments-touching update) ships to App Store + Play Store,
jtbds.iWantTo: confirm payment success rate ≥ 99% across the top device + OS combinations within 48 hours,
jtbds.soICan: catch a SDK-version-or-OS-version-specific bug before it shows up as 1-star reviews and uninstalls

metadata.frequency: 1–4× per year (major releases); additional minor releases monthly
metadata.actor: Mobile dev lead + Director of Payments
metadata.workaround: Mobile team checks Sentry + Crashlytics for pay-related crashes; payments team checks for transaction-volume anomaly per app-version
metadata.successMetric: Payment success rate ≥ 99% per major device-OS combination; no SDK-related crash > 0.1% rate per session
metadata.failureMode: SDK incompatibility on a recent OS version (e.g., iOS X.Y point-release breaks tokenization SDK) → app-store reviews drop, install rate drops, mobile-channel revenue contracts; also customer-trust loss
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per year for a brand with active mobile, a SDK-OS issue surfaces in production
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (Apple App Store reviews + Sentry public reports + 04-prd/mvp-scope.md Slice A)

jtbds.title: Verify in-store associates can complete a refund of a mobile-app or e-com purchase on day 1
jtbds.when: the omnichannel rollout's go-live moment arrives,
jtbds.iWantTo: test that an in-store associate can scan a mobile-app order or look up an e-com order, refund-to-original-card, and have the customer's account / loyalty / inventory updated correctly,
jtbds.soICan: prevent the day-1 PR disaster of "I bought online, you can't refund me in-store."

metadata.trigger: Phase boundary: omnichannel rollout `production_active` (typically tied to a marketing announcement)
metadata.frequency: 1× per major omnichannel launch; refresher quarterly
metadata.actor: Store Operations Manager + Director of Payments
metadata.workaround: Send out a 4-page PDF SOP; train one or two associates per store; cross fingers
metadata.successMetric: ≥ 95% of test refunds across stores succeed end-to-end on day 1; associate-error rate ≤ 5%
metadata.failureMode: Refund attempted at a store that hasn't been provisioned for cross-channel returns → associate manually issues store-credit; customer files a chargeback later for "double refund attempt"; merchant loses the chargeback because their evidence package doesn't match the gift-card reconciliation
metadata.failureFrequency: ~30% of omnichannel rollouts have at least one store with a misconfigured cross-channel refund flow on day 1
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (NRF returns benchmarks + Optoro 2024 cross-channel returns report)

jtbds.title: Detect a daily approval-rate dip on a single channel before it costs > 1% of daily volume
jtbds.when: approval rate on a single channel (e-com / POS / mobile) drops below the merchant's 30-day rolling baseline by more than 1.5pp for ≥ 1 hour,
jtbds.iWantTo: receive a Slack alert with the suspected root cause (BIN-range / decline-reason / APM / region) and a recommended next step (declined-cohort breakdown, vendor-side incident check, fallback APM),
jtbds.soICan: triage in minutes rather than discovering it via the next-day's exec dashboard

metadata.trigger: Threshold crossing: channel approval-rate Z-score ≤ -2 over a 1h rolling window vs 30d baseline
metadata.frequency: 2–6× per month (most are noise; 1–2 are real)
metadata.workaround: Custom Looker dashboard checked twice a day + Slack-bot for hard-coded thresholds; misses correlated multi-signal regressions
metadata.successMetric: Mean time from regression-start to first alert ≤ 30 minutes; root-cause hypothesis correct in ≥ 70% of confirmed-real alerts
metadata.failureMode: Late-detected approval-rate dip → revenue loss = (delta-pp × hourly-volume × hours-undetected). Typical: $5k–$50k per occurrence for a $100M-GPV brand
metadata.failureFrequency: ~1× per month a real regression goes undetected for 6+ hours
metadata.source: inferred-with-flag (Slice A success-metric: 30% approval-rate lift target — MVP scope.md)

jtbds.title: Daily settlement variance check vs POS shift report (per-store)
jtbds.when: the daily processor settlement file lands (typically 2–4am next-business-day),
jtbds.iWantTo: compare it to each store's POS shift report (gross sales − refunds − voids − tips) plus the e-com order ledger and flag any per-store variance > 0.5%,
jtbds.soICan: finance-team-close the day before 9am rather than chase variances mid-morning

metadata.trigger: Scheduled tick: daily 2:00 local; or webhook event: `settlement.delivered`

jtbds.iWantTo: auto-pull platform-aggregated evidence (delivery-tracking, IP-match, prior-fraud-flags),

jtbds.title: Seller-side dispute deduction with appeal-window
jtbds.when: chargeback determined to be seller-failure,

jtbds.title: Pre-arb evaluation for high-stakes platform-side disputes

jtbds.soICan: stop spending $200/case on weak ones

jtbds.title: Per-seller payout reconcile with held-funds + future-deductions

jtbds.iWantTo: auto-reconcile gross-sales − fees − held-funds − future-deductions = net-payout per seller,
jtbds.soICan: stop manual review of 50+ outliers

jtbds.title: 1099-K issuance per seller per state

jtbds.iWantTo: auto-issue per federal + state thresholds + e-file,

jtbds.title: Marketplace-tax-collection accounting (state-by-state)
jtbds.when: marketplace-collected sales-tax for buyers across 38 states,
jtbds.iWantTo: auto-categorize into liability accounts per state + remit on filing-cadence,
jtbds.soICan: stop the tax-team's quarterly nightmare

jtbds.title: Detect missing-payout cycle for high-volume seller
jtbds.when: top-50-seller's weekly payout doesn't run,
jtbds.iWantTo: alert "expected $48k payout to AcmeShoes — not initiated",

jtbds.title: Reconcile cross-border payouts with FX accounting

jtbds.title: Year-end platform 1099-K + tax recon

jtbds.title: Refund-rate anomaly per seller per category

jtbds.title: Customer-service refund-handling with multi-seller liability
jtbds.when: buyer requests refund via customer-service,
jtbds.iWantTo: auto-classify, allocate, draft response,
jtbds.soICan: stop CS-team manual handling

jtbds.title: Bulk-refund handling for product-recall scenarios

jtbds.soICan: stop assembling from 8 systems

jtbds.title: Seller-cohort-LTV analysis for tier-strategy

jtbds.soICan: target acquisition

jtbds.title: Buyer-cohort-LTV with recommendation-engine input
jtbds.when: I'm tuning the recommendation-engine,
jtbds.iWantTo: see buyer-LTV-by-purchase-pattern,
jtbds.soICan: prioritize recommendations

jtbds.title: Add new product category with payments + T&S setup
jtbds.when: I expand into "Watches" category,
jtbds.iWantTo: auto-configure category-specific payments + T&S + tax + counterfeit-risk-rules,
jtbds.soICan: stop new-category-launch taking 2 months

jtbds.title: International expansion (new country/jurisdiction)
jtbds.when: expanding to UK,
jtbds.iWantTo: auto-configure UK VAT + UK FX + UK seller-onboarding rules,
jtbds.soICan: stop UK-launch taking 6 months

jtbds.title: Complete PayFac KYC-Light during marketplace signup without form-fatigue
jtbds.when: I sign up as a seller on the marketplace and reach the "verify your identity" PayFac step,
jtbds.iWantTo: finish KYC in ≤5 minutes from one device with photo of my ID, EIN/SSN, and bank-account-link,
jtbds.soICan: stop getting stuck mid-flow and giving up on listing my products

jtbds.title: Multi-marketplace expansion without re-doing KYC from scratch
jtbds.when: I'm already verified on Marketplace A and want to expand to Marketplace B (both use the same PayFac),
jtbds.iWantTo: have B auto-recognize my A-side KYC and skip identity-verification (only require business-info + bank account),
jtbds.soICan: stop spending 5 days waiting for new KYC when I've already verified

jtbds.title: Connect own-site checkout to same PayFac via direct-API for advanced sellers
jtbds.when: I'm already selling on a marketplace and want to also accept payments on my own-site,
jtbds.iWantTo: generate a direct-API key from my PayFac dashboard and paste it into my own-site checkout SDK,
jtbds.soICan: reuse my existing PayFac account without re-doing boarding

jtbds.title: Auto-enroll in account-updater service to protect saved-card recurring sales
jtbds.when: I list a "subscribe & save" product (e.g., monthly art-print club) for $25/month,
jtbds.iWantTo: the PayFac to auto-enroll me in network-account-updater service for my vault tokens,
jtbds.soICan: stop losing 5–8% of subscription renewals to expired-card declines

jtbds.title: Marketplace-account-suspension warning + remediation plan
jtbds.when: I get a marketplace warning "you're at 1.45% dispute-rate; suspension risk",
jtbds.iWantTo: get a 30-day remediation plan tailored to my dispute-mix (listing-quality vs shipping vs item-not-received),
jtbds.soICan: stop guessing what to fix

jtbds.title: Marketplace-platform outage handling with cross-platform fallback
jtbds.when: my primary marketplace has a 60-minute checkout-outage,
jtbds.iWantTo: the system flag it AND auto-redirect my Pinterest ads to my secondary marketplace + own-site,
jtbds.soICan: stop losing high-ad-spend traffic to dead checkout

jtbds.title: Annual marketplace-fee-comparison for platform mix decision
jtbds.when: my annual seller-membership renewal hits ($199/year for one platform),
jtbds.iWantTo: see "your effective fee-rate on Platform A is 7.8% vs Platform B 6.2% — consider re-balancing volume",
jtbds.soICan: make platform-mix decisions with data instead of inertia

jtbds.title: First-payout reconcile after marketplace fee + PayFac fee + reserve deduction
jtbds.when: my first payout hits my bank for $487 (vs. $640 in gross sales),
jtbds.iWantTo: see "$640 gross − $96 marketplace fee − $44 PayFac fee − $13 rolling reserve = $487 expected" in one summary,
jtbds.soICan: stop wondering "where did $153 go?" and trust the system

jtbds.title: Verify drop-in checkout widget passes pre-launch test on marketplace listing
jtbds.when: I'm 24 hours from going live with my first marketplace listing,
jtbds.iWantTo: trigger a $0.01 pre-auth from my own browser via the drop-in checkout widget and confirm round-trip + auto-void,
jtbds.soICan: know before my first real buyer that the widget is configured correctly

jtbds.title: Configure rolling-reserve thresholds and release schedule with seller education
jtbds.when: PayFac applies a 5% rolling-reserve hold on my account due to my new-seller status,
jtbds.iWantTo: see "5% held for 90 days; releases on $X cadence; expected to drop to 2% after 90-day clean period",
jtbds.soICan: plan my cash flow without surprises

jtbds.title: Multi-marketplace daily-orders-summary across platforms
jtbds.when: I sell on Etsy-class + Shopify-class + own-site,
jtbds.iWantTo: see one "today: 14 orders ($487 gross)" across all 3 platforms with per-platform breakdown,
jtbds.soICan: stop logging into 3 dashboards every morning

jtbds.title: Detect held/rolled-back funds with explanation and resolution path
jtbds.when: PayFac places a 24-hour hold on a $400 transaction (high-risk-velocity flag),
jtbds.iWantTo: get an alert "transaction held — high-velocity flag; provide tracking + customer-service-history to release",
jtbds.soICan: respond same-day instead of finding out 3 days later when my payout is short

jtbds.title: Detect counterfeit / IP-infringement risk on listings before takedown
jtbds.when: my new product listing matches a trademarked term I didn't realize was protected (e.g., "Marvel-style necklace"),
jtbds.iWantTo: get a flag "listing risks IP takedown — review or rename" before it goes live,
jtbds.soICan: stop my account being suspended for IP-infringement

jtbds.title: Auto-block card-testing attacks against marketplace checkout
jtbds.when: I see 6 declined authorizations in 90 seconds from rotating cards on the same IP attacking my listing,
jtbds.iWantTo: the gateway to auto-block that IP for 4 hours,
jtbds.soICan: stop card-testing inflating my decline rate and triggering PayFac risk review

jtbds.title: Auto-handle order-refund within marketplace SLA via PayFac
jtbds.when: a buyer requests refund for "item not as described" within the marketplace 30-day window,
jtbds.iWantTo: auto-process the refund through PayFac with the marketplace's mediation policy applied,
jtbds.soICan: stop the buyer escalating to a chargeback that costs me a $15 fee

jtbds.title: Detect inventory-payment sync drift (sold but reserved-funds)
jtbds.when: I sold an item Saturday but the funds are still in PayFac reserve on Tuesday,
jtbds.iWantTo: see "12 of last 30 sales held in reserve — total $487; $312 releases tomorrow",
jtbds.soICan: plan inventory replenishment without guessing on cash availability

jtbds.title: Auto-classify "item not as described" dispute and recommend response
jtbds.when: a chargeback notification arrives with reason code 4855 / 13.1 (item-not-as-described),
jtbds.iWantTo: see "recommend DEFEND — listing has 4 photos + dimension specs + delivered with signature" or "recommend ACCEPT — buyer-rating-pattern shows valid complaint",
jtbds.soICan: stop wasting 30 minutes per dispute pulling evidence manually

jtbds.title: Surface dispute deadline urgency
jtbds.when: a dispute deadline is ≤48 hours away (PayFac flows have shorter windows than direct),
jtbds.iWantTo: get an SMS+push "dispute deadline 36 hours, draft ready, tap to send",
jtbds.soICan: stop missing PayFac-mediated dispute deadlines

jtbds.title: Track marketplace-dispute-rate threshold for account-suspension prevention
jtbds.when: my marketplace-dispute-rate over 60 days approaches 1.5% (typical marketplace SOR threshold),
jtbds.iWantTo: see "you're at 1.2% — top reasons: item-quality (5) + late-shipping (3) — review listings",
jtbds.soICan: stop a slow drift before triggering marketplace account-suspension

jtbds.title: Prevent dispute via proactive buyer-issue-resolution
jtbds.when: a buyer messages me complaining about late shipping,
jtbds.iWantTo: auto-draft an apology + tracking-update + 10% off-next-order before they file a dispute,
jtbds.soICan: stop disputes-from-unhappy-buyers-who-would-have-settled-by-message

jtbds.title: Multi-platform payout consolidation into single accounting view
jtbds.when: I get separate payouts from Etsy ($487), Shopify ($812), and own-site ($203),
jtbds.iWantTo: see "this week: $1,502 net across 3 platforms — gross $1,847, marketplace fees $245, PayFac fees $61, refunds $39",
jtbds.soICan: stop spending 4 hours/week reconciling 3 dashboards

jtbds.title: Detect rolling-reserve rate-bump before it impacts payouts

jtbds.iWantTo: get a heads-up "reserve increasing — driven by 3 disputes in last 30 days; recommend listing-quality review",

jtbds.title: Detect missing payout cycle (delayed beyond normal cadence)

jtbds.title: Year-end 1099-K reconciliation across multiple platforms

jtbds.soICan: stop the accountant treating 1099-K as the only number

jtbds.title: Auto-flag refund-rate anomaly at SKU level
